_note: Admission cards for gates BORN AFTER 2026-08-23. Read by hooks/gate-edit-gate.py, which refuses a NEW blocking gate whose card is absent or incomplete. A matcher that only announces needs no card: this prices the power to refuse work, never the work of building a check.
_why: The 2026-08-23 gates-audit council (out/council/gates-audit-20260823/) found the system running 59 named controls, born one reasonable afternoon at a time, with gate-edit re-blessing hashes and nothing anywhere asking whether the next control should be able to stop a session. Grok's chair, high confidence: 'This is the missing gate that prevents the next 59 from becoming 90.'
_grandfathered: Every gate already in ops/config/gate-baseline.json on 2026-08-23 keeps its place with no card. That is deliberate, not an oversight: a check that failed on day one across forty-odd existing gates would be muted on day one, which is the failure ops/enforcement-coverage-check.py documents at length and answers the same way. The debt is real and belongs to the telemetry sentence the same council ordered, not to a wall in front of today's work.

_questions.parent_incident: the dated incident where prose failed. Either this or landing_harm is required; a recitation of a taught rule is not parentage.
_questions.landing_harm: one sentence: if this does not bind, WHICH artifact lands in WHOSE hands. 'Could be bad' does not qualify.
_questions.bind_moment: the last cheap reversible moment before that harm. A true rule at the wrong moment is a tax.
_questions.consumer: who receives the wrong artifact. If the only consumer is the gate's own log, the gate is sediment.
_questions.self_serve_remedy: what a refused session can DO, without a new login. A dead end fails even when the rule is right.
_questions.scarce_resource_cost: what it spends, in order of scarcity: Joe's and Dell's attention, this Mac's wall-clock under parallel sessions, Stop-reopen tokens, billed CI minutes.
_questions.unique_bind: why nothing already binds this class at this moment. Two blockers on one claim-set fail uniqueness.
_questions.matcher_test: a repo-relative fixture path that EXISTS, written before the gate (rule e65efc68). A card naming a test nobody wrote is the box-ticking version of this control.

context-handoff-gate.py.parent_incident: On 2026-08-30 transcript a8e1daa6-3c72-4334-9d13-f52f4a9be88e crossed 1,013,084 tokens, auto-compacted to 38,496, and the later Stop invocation silently allowed because it saw only postcompact usage.
context-handoff-gate.py.landing_harm: Without a verified successor receipt, a source task can compact or terminate while its unfinished repository ownership, decisions, and exact next action exist on no active surface.
context-handoff-gate.py.bind_moment: The Stop boundary after the configured soft or hard threshold, while the source task can still complete a same-task ownership transfer.
context-handoff-gate.py.consumer: The successor task and dispatcher that must continue the same CARR System OS slice without duplicate or missing ownership.
context-handoff-gate.py.self_serve_remedy: Create and pin a same-slice successor; bind controller-captured native identity evidence to the immutable offer, declaration, receipt, and final through this gate's CLI; read the records back; then retry Stop after TAKEOVER_VERIFIED. A dispatcher recovery can instead be completed by the same handoff flow or explicitly aborted to restore the predecessor.
context-handoff-gate.py.scarce_resource_cost: One reopened model turn only after a measured threshold or conservative fallback cap; PostToolUse notices are one-shot and PreCompact never blocks.
context-handoff-gate.py.unique_bind: No other gate preserves precompact high-water, validates cross-surface ownership and evidence bindings, detects stale worker heartbeats, or refuses Stop until the exact predecessor-to-successor takeover is verified.

rule-boot-gate.py.parent_incident: On 2026-09-26 the rule-delivery audit found that no SessionStart hook loaded any rule: 195 active rules existed, and a session or subagent reached its first tool call having read none of them unless it chose to call standing-context. Joe demanded 100% recall of relevant rules.
rule-boot-gate.py.landing_harm: A session or subagent acts (edits, commits, sends, spawns) without having read the always-on rules or the index that tells it which rule applies, so a known rule is broken for want of being read.
rule-boot-gate.py.bind_moment: PreToolUse on every tool, from SessionStart (startup, resume, clear, compact, fork) or subagent start until that context has every page of standing-context detail=boot for the armed digest confirmed (PostToolUse reads each fetch's answer; a new digest or page count re-arms the session).
rule-boot-gate.py.consumer: The session or subagent itself: the always-on full text and the rule index land in its own context before it acts.
rule-boot-gate.py.self_serve_remedy: Make the calls the deny names: standing-context {"detail":"boot","page":N} for each missing page, over the CARR MCP connector or as `./run.sh call standing-context '{"detail":"boot","page":N}'`. The fetch is always allowed. No context can be locked out: a fetch that errors unlocks it with RULES UNAVAILABLE; a Worker that does not serve the boot yet holds nothing (RULE BOOT NOT DEPLOYED YET); a hold that cannot be recorded is not made (STATE UNWRITABLE); and after 3 holds without progress the gate stops holding that context (RULES UNREAD).
rule-boot-gate.py.scarce_resource_cost: About 34k tokens of rule text per context, once per session start or subagent, plus at most 3 denied calls per context. The hook reads a few marker files on each call and parses the fetch answer on PostToolUse: no network, no model.
rule-boot-gate.py.unique_bind: No other gate stops a context from acting before it has read the rules; SessionStart context is capped at 10,000 characters, so the rules cannot be pushed in, and every other rule-delivery path is advisory.

github-burst-guard.py.parent_incident: On 2026-10-06 a session ran a shell loop making about 55 gh calls within seconds, then ran ops/release-pipeline.py tick by hand three times in five minutes. GitHub's short-window (secondary) rate limit answered 403 for the shared account and an urgent production release stopped behind the lockout. Joe ordered a rule (74ddb23c, never burst GitHub) and enforcement.
github-burst-guard.py.landing_harm: A 403 lockout of the one GitHub account every session, CI watcher, review loop and the release pipeline share, which stops merges and production releases for everyone until GitHub lifts it.
github-burst-guard.py.bind_moment: PreToolUse on Bash, before the burst command runs: a gh loop or xargs/parallel fan-out with no sleep of 2s or more, a release tick or shepherd run while a tick holds the pipeline's single-run lock (out/release-pipeline/lock, probed with a non-blocking flock; --help, -h and report are not ticks), or any gh call within 15 minutes of a recorded rate-limit answer (recorded on PostToolUse/PostToolUseFailure from a GitHub-touching command's output).
github-burst-guard.py.consumer: The session issuing the command, and through the shared account every other session and the release pipeline, which would otherwise receive the 403.
github-burst-guard.py.self_serve_remedy: Every refusal names the cheaper call: one gh api --paginate or gh api graphql call instead of a per-item loop, or a sleep of 2s or more inside the loop; retry the tick as soon as the running one releases its lock, or read the pipeline's state instead of ticking it; during the cooldown, gh api rate_limit stays allowed and shows when the limit resets. A short literal list (items x gh calls per pass <= 10) and an until-gh poll with a sleep pass unrefused.
github-burst-guard.py.scarce_resource_cost: One more hook process per Bash call (a Python cold start under hook-meter-run.py), then a regex pass over the command and one small state-file read when the command runs gh or the release tick. No network, no model, no Stop reopen. A refusal costs one model turn to rewrite the command.
github-burst-guard.py.unique_bind: No other gate looks at GitHub call volume: guard-unattended.py refuses destructive and exfiltrating commands and the egress allowlist, and nothing records a rate-limit answer or spaces release ticks.
